messages:
Alex Rivera: Heads up — we started seeing a ~20-30ms per-token tail-latency regression on the 13B nightly after the fused-attn kernel landing. P95 jumped from ~45ms -> ~70ms on xlatency tests. perf-bot flagged it at 07:12.
Maria Chen: ugh. Do we have before/after microbench numbers? seq lengths and batch shapes?
Alex Rivera: Yep. Attach quick numbers I ran on a stable host:
```
Baseline (flash_v2, pre-commit abc123): seq=512, batch=1, tokens/sec=410, p95=45ms
After (fused_v1, post-commit def456): seq=512, batch=1, tokens/sec=280, p95=70ms
Large seq (seq=1024): baseline p95=90ms, after p95=130ms
```
Also instrumented with nvprof/trace showing additional memcpy and kernel fallback spikes.
Ryan Patel: Can you paste the tracer flame/stack? Is it hitting a slow path in KV cache copy or the attention kernel itself?
Alex Rivera: Pasting key pieces. Trace shows a long memcpy (~8ms) right before attention call in the fused path. NVTX:
```
[...]->prepare_kv_cache (0.2ms)
[...]->kv_cache_update (8.1ms memcpy)
[...]->fused_attention_kernel_launcher (12.4ms)
```
Whereas baseline flash path has no big memcpy and attention kernel is ~9ms.
Samira Gupta: Sounds like paged-attn path is materializing tensors into contiguous buffers for fused kernel. We had a similar regression in Feb where alignment caused an extra .contiguous() copy.
Maria Chen: Good call. Was the fused kernel expecting specific stride/alignment? Any autotune/kernel selection fallback logged?
Alex Rivera: The runtime logs show kernel selection: fused_v1 chosen for seq<=1024, but the selection logic doesn't check tensor.stride/contiguity — it assumes contiguous inputs. If not contiguous, we call aten::contiguous which triggers the memcpy. commit def456 added fused_v1 as default which probably didn't account for builder-level padding.
perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression detected on model: 13B-nightly, metric: p95_token_latency, delta: +55% between abc123 -> def456. See /perf/alerts/1749005
Ryan Patel: Ok bisect plan: git bisect between abc123..def456 + run small microbench reproducer that prints kernel selection & nvtx. Can you run local bisect script and dump first bad commit?
Alex Rivera: Starting git bisect now. Script: `./eng/runtime/tools/perf_bisect.sh --microbench=attn_seq512 --repeats=5 --record=nvtx`.
Alex Rivera: Update: git bisect points to commit def456 (the fused-attn enablement). The exact change: runtime/kernel_selector: prefer fused_v1 for short seqs. The change also added `torch.as_contiguous_tensor` before kernel call for safety.
Samira Gupta: That explains the memcpy. as_contiguous_tensor will always allocate and copy. We should prefer to update kernel selector to avoid fused_v1 when tensors aren't contiguous OR adjust builder to produce contiguous-backed tensors without copy.
Maria Chen: Quick experiment: can you rerun two variants — 1) disable fused_v1, 2) keep fused_v1 but skip the as_contiguous_tensor call (risky) — and show perf numbers?
Alex Rivera: Ran both
```
Disable fused_v1 (force flash_v2): p95=46ms tokens/sec=405
Fused_v1 without as_contiguous_tensor (force use, assume inputs contiguous): p95=54ms tokens/sec=360
Fused_v1 with as_contiguous_tensor (current): p95=70ms tokens/sec=280
```
So fused_v1 can be competitive if inputs are already contiguous. The copy kills it.
Ryan Patel: Two mitigation paths: (A) revert fused_v1 as default until builder produces contiguous buffers; (B) update builder to ensure contiguous layout upstream (maybe during KV cache writes) and add a cheap contiguity check in selector to avoid calling as_contiguous on noncontig tensors.
Samira Gupta: Also we should add a heuristic to kernel selector: if a contiguous check fails, prefer flash_v2 unless fused_v1 shows net benefit after measuring copy cost (we can estimate cost based on number of elements).
infra-bot: Canary job scheduled: eng-runtime/canary/attn-latency-13b at 08:30. Will compare abc123 vs candidate.
Maria Chen: What about batching heuristics? Any interaction with the batcher window that could amplify memcpy frequency?
Alex Rivera: Yes — continuous batching with prefix KV caching causes frequent small updates to KV buffers. If we allocate contiguous scratch buffers per request for fused_v1, cost multiplies. The builder currently appends KV pages with padding which is noncontiguous in certain sharding layouts.
Ryan Patel: OK. Action items:
- Revert default selection change (rollback PR) for immediate mitigation (owner: Alex)
- Add contiguity check in kernel selector and cost-model estimate for copy vs kernel win (owner: Samira)
- Adjust KV builder to emit contiguous-backed pages when possible (owner: Ryan)
- Add microbench unit that asserts no extra as_contiguous_tensor calls for normal batch shapes (owner: Maria)
- Canary and perf alerts will monitor (infra-bot)
Alex Rivera: I've opened PR #4321 to revert the selector change and posted the bisect log + nvtx traces. Putting a note to include the microbench output in the PR description.
Maria Chen: For the long-term, we should instrument the runtime to emit a metric: attention_kernel_copy_time and attention_kernel_choice per request. That will help root-cause regressions fast. Also add an eval threshold that fails CI if p95 regresses >10% on the microbench suite.
Samira Gupta: Agree. I'll draft the selector patch with a cheap contiguous check (torch.is_contiguous) and an estimated copy_cost = elems * bytes_per_elem / mem_bandwidth, compare to expected kernel delta.
Ryan Patel: Also test paged attention toggles — sometimes paged attention reduces memory live set and avoids copies. Can you add a matrix test: flash_v2/fused_v1 x paged_on/off x seq 256/512/1024.
Alex Rivera: Will run matrix overnight and drop results in /eng/runtime/perf/1749005123-attn-bisect.
perf-bot: [info] New canary run scheduled. Baseline abc123 vs candidate def456-rollback will be compared. Thresholds: p95_delta 10%.
Alex Rivera: Quick summary in case folks join later: root cause is as_contiguous_tensor copy introduced as safety before fused kernel. Copy + frequent KV updates caused large p95 regressions. Immediate revert rolled back selection; next step is smarter selector & builder fixes, and more microbench coverage.
Maria Chen: Thanks — set up a follow-up sync tomorrow 09:30 to track PRs and canary results. :+1:
Samira Gupta: I'll add the selection unit tests and the cost model prototype by EOD.
Ryan Patel: I'll prototype builder contiguity change and run heavy batch integration tests.
Alex Rivera: Thanks all. Leaving traces & bisect artifacts in the perf dir. ping me if you want realtime logs.
perf-bot: [resolved] incident perf-regression-1749005: mitigation applied (revert deployed).
